Petro Home Services vs Bottini Fuel

Neither posts a per-gallon price on its own site. Petro sets out its plan terms; Bottini's published figures come from the Mid-Hudson Fuel Buyers Community, read 2026-11-19.

How to choose

In the Hudson Valley, the Mid-Hudson buyers' group is the only route to a published Bottini price, and its enrollment runs once a year in July and August. Outside it, ask both dealers for a quote on the same day and compare each with the New York EIA average. On a ceiling or cap plan, ask what the plan costs: Petro charges nothing up front but $399 to leave early; the Mid-Hudson Bottini cap charges $0.35/gal up front.

FAQ

Is Bottini cheaper than Petro?
Neither posts a per-gallon price on its own site, so a direct comparison needs a quote from each. The one published Bottini figure is the Mid-Hudson Fuel Buyers Community's 2026-27 member price: $4.399/gal fixed or capped (the cap adds a $0.35/gal enrollment cost), for members who enrolled by 7 August 2026.
Does Petro charge a fee for its Ceiling plan?
Petro says its pricing plans have no enrollment or sign-up fees. The Ceiling plan needs a one-year commitment, and leaving early costs a $399 early termination fee.
Where do they overlap?
Bottini serves Hudson Valley counties (Ulster, Dutchess, Orange, Sullivan, Delaware, Greene, Columbia). Petro lists a Poughkeepsie office among its New York offices, so Dutchess County households can ask both.
